candidate_relations.reason: The C7–T1 mass causes marked canal stenosis, so spinal stenosis is the compressive consequence rather than a hemorrhagic synovial cyst.
A well-circumscribed extra-axial lesion with no internal enhancement and intact bone is not typical spinal metastasis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: spinal metastasis vs rim-only extra-axial cyst

candidate_relations.reason: Neurofibroma should enhance internally and is usually T2-bright, unlike this homogeneously T2-low, rim-only-enhancing extra-axial mass.
Neoplasm as a generic solid tumor conflicts with thin rim enhancement, no internal enhancement, and uniformly low T2 signal from blood products.
The mass is extra-axial and posterolateral to the cord, not an intrinsic spinal cord tumor.
Spastic paraparesis, T7 sensory level, and cord deformation are spinal cord compression, the neurologic effect of the cyst.
Hemangioma of bone lives in the vertebra; this lesion is extra-axial beside the cord at C7–T1.
Hemangiopericytoma is an avidly enhancing extra-axial tumor, opposite of rim-only enhancement without internal enhancement.
Lipoma is T1-bright fat; this mass is intermediate on T1 and homogeneously low on T2.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: lipoma vs intermediate T1 / low T2

candidate_relations.reason: Facet degenerative disease is the usual setting for synovial cysts but the label omits the hemorrhagic synovial cyst itself.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: degenerative family missing hemorrhagic synovial cyst

candidate_relations.reason: Schwannoma is an enhancing extra-axial nerve-sheath tumor, not a T2-uniformly-dark lesion with only a thin enhancing rim.
Meningioma typically enhances homogeneously; rim-only enhancement and homogeneously low T2 signal favor hemorrhage in a cyst over meningioma.
Spinal cord metastasis would be intra-axial or osseous, not a posterolateral extra-axial T2-dark cystic mass.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: cord metastasis vs extra-axial hemorrhagic cyst
